items.title: Angular-search saturation at fixed output count
items.summary: Proposed question: does wider rotational search improve rank1 and best50 DockQ when retained count stays 50 and complete-workflow budgets match? MEGADOCK documents 3,600 versus 54,000 rotations; these establish search sizes, not a quality scaling law (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md).
items.root_link: Bears directly on additional-search recovery and affordability, extending D/G comparison into search-saturation study (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-1649-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md#problem-definition).
items.compute_open: More parallel compute buys search width: largest rotation count documented by cited guide is 54,000, without a measured quality-versus-width curve; whether larger or differently distributed angular sets improve rank1 or best50 remains unknown and requires an explicit sampler extension (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md).
items.sequential: none: rotations already distribute across CPU threads and GPUs, so 54,000 rotations are independent search tasks, with local voxelization/FFT/solution dependencies rather than 54,000 dependent timesteps (https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btu532). Proposed comparison needs four cases × two widths = eight docking runs per execution block; single-run GPU busy fraction remains unreported for these inputs, and further distribution pays only when work exceeds dispatch/merge overhead—existing MEGADOCK rotation distribution supplies nearest demonstrated implementation (https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btu532).
items.narrowing: Leaves agreement margins, provenance and controller repair aside; angular coverage tests rigid-body sampling sufficiency, while signed rank1/best50 effects test useful recovery under sealed budgets.
